changelogEntry10:
- The reader now shows chronicle achievements and story endings: unlocking a compendium achievement prints a "Chronicle achievement" toast with the unlocked name, and opening the ending panel renders a "Story ending" card, falling back to the raw id when the name is missing.
- Story endings now use their own paper card: horizontal text, thin border, centered crimson title flanked by rules, and justified body text, instead of the vertical death-ending block. Reading settings gain a dedicated "Story ending" text type for its font and typesetting.
- The filter gains "Chronicle" and "Story ending" fields that match by name or id; the death-ending field, block and text type now share the "Death ending" label.
- Meta chips without a lookup target can be selected and copied, while hidden chips keep their peek behavior.
changelogEntry9:
- Slimmed the desktop masthead and rail: no close or search buttons between the filter button and the language picker, and no rail toggle or close button when the outline is docked; responsive visibility rules were being overridden by the base button style, so framework toggles now live in their own layer.
- The mobile usage guide keeps only touch gestures and filter syntax; the keyboard-only navigation and reading groups are hidden.
- Fixed returning to the last reading position: positions are recorded as a nested path plus an offset inside the block, and options, condition branches, jumps and battle reports are expanded before aligning, so scripts holding a single choice block such as ch1_1_break_option return to the original line inside the branch on both desktop and mobile.
- The lookup panel renders in batches and caches first lines, so opening and scrolling stay fast with thousands of hits while group counts and empty states are unchanged.
- The version info in More now lists the game version and build number, matching the line under the masthead title, and shows unknown when the data is missing.
- Fixed the lookup panel refreshing in place without moving when another lookup was opened while it was already open: switching triggers now re-anchors the panel to the new element, while clicks inside the panel and repeat clicks on the same trigger keep it in place.
- Fixed the filter panel not opening from the mobile search row: the row now stays expanded while the filter panel is open, and closing the filter or the row's close button collapses both.
- The mobile top bar now toggles on tapping empty space in the story text instead of hiding and reappearing on scroll.
changelogEntry8:
- Fixed search jumps and previous/next history jumps failing to return to the last reading position: the reader restores by the block at the top of the viewport plus the offset inside it, and search positioning is no longer overridden by the restore.
- Fixed lookup and other floating panels overflowing the viewport when opened near a window edge: panels are clamped into the viewport by their real size with a safe margin and scroll internally when too tall.
- Mobile layout: the masthead is a single row with the current script id after the rail button, search opens as an icon-triggered row, and all reader actions sit directly in the bar; the top chrome hides while reading down and returns on any scroll up.
changelogEntry7:
- Battle and duel cards now render their titles, goals, status, forces, triggers and actions in the interface language, so the Simplified Chinese and English readers no longer mix in Traditional Chinese labels.
- The More menu gains version info: the py and web versions plus the git commit the site was built from, with the short hash linking to GitHub.
- Condition inference and flag inference are merged into a single Inference toggle (F) using the logical entailment icon; the C shortcut is gone.
- Lookup conditions no longer show return values, and each branch is separated by a divider.
- The group font default in reading settings is back to Follow base instead of showing base; saved reading preferences are reset once.
- Fixed the expression bubble in the top-right corner of speaker portraits being clipped.
- Mission state labels use a slash instead of the old arrow separator, exported text uses ASCII separators, and the empty state and inference marks use inline icons.
- Off-screen rows skip rendering and locale messages are precompiled, so first load and scrolling cost less.
changelogEntry1:
- The reading page adds a display filter left of flag inference for dialogue, inner voice, narration and biographies; it affects story text only, leaves battle cards intact, and resets on reload.
- A tri-state fold button sits right of the display filter: it expands or collapses all options and condition branches at once, collapsing when everything is open, expanding when everything is closed, and following the expanded majority otherwise; battle cards stay untouched.
- The catalogue rail is laid out like a printed contents page, with chapter and script totals, ordinals, colour marks, per-chapter counts and clearer expand arrows.
- Rail search is kept when switching tabs, its hint now reads "Filter scripts…", and matches are counted while searching.
- Bookmark delete buttons appear only on hover or focus and sit further inside the row.
- Branch hover previews are gone from the reader; branches open on click.
- The masthead shows only the game version, dropping the generation time and build number, and the search box is centred over the reader column.
- Talent changes read as learned or forgotten with the level always positive.
- "Scene script / combat event" markers are gone from the reader breadcrumb and rail entries, along with the filter's source field and its system and scene kinds.
changelogEntry2:
- The reader shows a character portrait and expression left of the speaker name, with a settings toggle and size control.
- A local framing workbench (pnpm framing) pans and zooms the avatar frame per character and expression with a live mirrored preview; the result is written to data/portrait-framing.json and reused by every extraction, while untouched expressions keep the default crop.
changelogEntry3:
- Portraits now show only when the speaker is actually on screen: off screen lines, exits and view transitions leave an empty dashed frame instead, with a hover hint that the character is not on screen.
- A line followed straight away by the speaker walking back into view keeps its portrait; lines spoken several beats before the entrance no longer regain one.
- Conditional and choice branches, exits, view transitions and characters peeking up from below the screen are all taken into account, so far fewer lines show a portrait for someone off screen or miss one for someone on screen.
changelogEntry4:
- Font selection is rebuilt: the picker lists only fonts installed on this machine, shows Chinese names with the Latin family name beside them, and matches Chinese, English and aliases alike; denied permissions, insecure addresses and unsupported browsers now explain themselves.
- Text types gain a base font: every group and type set to follow the base uses it, and the default stays the serif stack.
- Header search no longer requires two characters, so a single character searches the text right away.
changelogEntry5:
- A dark theme arrives: the first row of the reading settings switches between light, dark and system, defaults to system, and keeps the choice on this device; while following the system, a change of the system appearance applies right away.
- The masthead, contents rail, story text, overlays and every panel change together: in the dark theme the text sits on warm brown-black paper in rice white, accents turn into muted amber gold, and the seal and ending colours are brightened to match.
- The theme is applied before the first paint, so dark readers no longer see a flash of light.
- Mood bubbles at the top-right of the speaker portrait now cover the full game set: happy (laugh), nervous (nervous1-3), angry, shy, shock and silent each get their own mark, while expressions with no game art (sad, hurt, gloomy, special and so on) stay bare; the marks reuse the game sprites, mirrored and shown statically.
- The mood marks are no longer standalone PNG files: all of them are packed into the first avatar atlas page and the reader locates them through the atlas, so no extra image requests are made; the manifest is now requested with the atlas version and revalidated, so a stale cached manifest can no longer blank every portrait after an atlas upgrade.
- Portrait size now defaults to 80px and can be adjusted between 60 and 100px.
- Search now matches per line: every matching line gets its own candidate, the snippet is the matched line itself, and picking it jumps straight to that line, so several matches inside one script are all reachable.
- The interface is unified throughout: slimmer shell and overlays, tab-style catalogue rows that merge into one card when expanded, word counts grouped into per-chapter cards with fully clickable rows, expand chevrons moved left of the labels, a settings drawer that previews the font of every text type and scrolls sideways, and the shortcut panel renamed to a usage guide.
changelogEntry6:
- Script export is fixed: each chapter is exported as plain text and packed into a ZIP, the More menu downloads it directly, a README records the chapter and script counts with the generation details, and the export loads all text and checkpoint data first, retries the shards that fail to load, skips scripts without text and keeps raw checkpoint references when checkpoints are missing.
- Filter values now match exactly: speaker:girl1 only finds the speaker girl1 itself, while the suggestion list still searches values by fragment.
- The filter suggestion list takes the arrow keys: the highlight wraps and scrolls into view, Enter or Tab confirms, and completing a field swaps the list straight to that field's values, including when a field chip is clicked.
- The filter fields are trimmed to speaker, flag, checkpoint, stat, affinity, death ending and chapter; flag candidates show inferred names that also work for search and filtering, with the full name on hover, while the hit count keeps only its number and the examples and usage guide follow suit.
- The filter gains a mission field covering missions and mission states: type either name to find the scripts that trigger it, and mission labels read "Mission ▷ State" without ids in parentheses.
- Mission names on trigger and end events are now lookup chips with an underline on hover; the panel shows only the mission state id and the scripts that trigger it, or the mission id and the scripts that end it, without expanding the state details.
- The jump panel includes mission triggers and after-battle continuations in both directions: a mission state's start script lists its triggers, scripts that continue after a battle or duel read "After-battle script", the badges read "Mission" and "After", and every badge drops its border and background.
- Scene switches in the reader no longer show raw names such as Free, Title and Story: they read "Back to free roaming", "Back to title screen" and "Continue the story", the after-battle destination on battle cards follows the same wording, and unrecognised scenes keep their raw name.
- Dynamic jumps in the reader no longer show raw Lua like SetNextScript(var1): temp script slots list every script that wrote to the slot, travel scripts are narrowed by their upstream writers, a single destination becomes a direct link, several go into a collapsible list, and unresolved ones read as decided at runtime.
- Time marks in the reader can be selected and copied.
